title: Male pelvis & perineum anatomy
description: The male pelvic floor in sagittal section: bladder, prostate and urethra in front, rectum and anal canal behind, and the muscular sheet that holds them up.

questions.question: Which organs are located in the male pelvis?
questions.answer: The male pelvis contains bladder, prostate and rectum, along with parts of the urethra, reproductive ducts, pelvic vessels and nerves.

questions.question: What is the pelvic floor's role in men?
questions.answer: Pelvic-floor muscles support pelvic organs and contribute to continence. Their relationship to the urethra and perineal structures is important in regional anatomy.

questions.question: Where is the urinary bladder in the male pelvis?
questions.answer: Reservoir behind the pubis. Function: Stores urine; trigone is its smooth base.

questions.question: Where is the prostatic & membranous urethra located?
questions.answer: Urethra traversing prostate and perineum. Function: Conduit for urine and semen; sphincters here.

questions.question: What is the function of the rectum?
questions.answer: Function: Stores stool before defecation. Terminal 12–15 cm with three valves.
